holidays.name: National Black Cat Day
holidays.description: A day to show some love to the sleek, shadowy cats that get an unfair reputation every fall. Adopt one, donate to a shelter, or just give your favorite panther-in-miniature an extra scritch.
holidays.origin: The day grew out of a push to counter the superstitions that make black cats harder to adopt, especially around Halloween. It is an unofficial observance, and it lands right as spooky season peaks.
holidays.funFact: Black cats are often adopted less quickly than cats of other colors. In some places, such as parts of the UK and Japan, they are considered symbols of good luck.

holidays.name: Cranky Co-Workers Day
holidays.description: This is a day for sighing at the office kettle and extending a little grace to the grumpiest person on your team. Try bringing the office grouch a coffee, or at least don't take that 9 a.m. scowl personally.
holidays.origin: Ruth and Thomas Roy of Wellcat Holidays created it. The couple is known for inventing lighthearted, offbeat observances.
holidays.funFact: Wellcat Holidays is behind many cheerful, quirky calendar days. Cranky Co-Workers Day is one of the few that gently encourages kindness toward a bad mood.

holidays.name: National American Beer Day
holidays.description: A toast to homegrown brews, from craft IPAs to classic lagers. It's a good excuse to try a beer from a small local brewery you haven't visited yet.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial food and drink observance, and its origin is unclear. It is listed on October 27 each year.
holidays.funFact: The U.S. has thousands of craft breweries, so you could drink a different local beer on this day for years without repeating one.
